meta.title: Propose your token as Frankencoin collateral
meta.description: How token issuers list a new collateral on Frankencoin: proposal fee, initialization period, FCS veto and what makes a good collateral.

hero.title: Let your holders borrow francs|against your token.
hero.subtitle: Anyone can propose a new collateral. A proposal costs 1'000 ZCHF and can be vetoed by Frankencoin Shares (FCS) holders for at least five days; if nobody vetoes, it goes live. Talk to us before you propose.

items.title: Discuss first
items.body: Share your token and the terms you have in mind with the community. Proposals that were discussed are far more likely to pass.

items.title: Propose
items.body: Open the first position with your terms in the app. The 1'000 ZCHF proposal fee goes to the reserve and is not refunded.

items.title: Review and veto period
items.body: For at least five days, FCS holders review the proposal and can veto it. If no one does, the collateral is live and others can borrow against it.

criteria.title: What reviewers look for
items: A liquid market: auctions must be able to sell the token quickly if a position is challenged.
Conservative terms: a liquidation price well below the market price gives the system room in a crash.
A transparent issuer: clear legal structure and public information about the asset behind the token.
A sensible limit: start small; the limit can be raised later with a new proposal.

guidance.title: Assessment guidance
guidance.body: A proposal sets the liquidation price, minting limit, interest, maturity and reserve share. Existing assessments show how the community weighs these parameters and the rights attached to a token; read a few before you choose yours.

faq.a: Anyone with 1'000 ZCHF for the fee and enough of the token for the initial position. No registration or approval is needed.
The community, in public. Discussion happens on [Telegram](https://t.me/frankencoinzchf) and in written assessments on [collateral.frankencoin.com](https://collateral.frankencoin.com/).

faq.q: Who can veto, and what happens then?
faq.a: FCS holders with more than 1% of voting power, including delegated votes. A vetoed proposal is denied and the fee stays in the reserve; you can propose again with different terms.
